newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA QUALIFY FOR OCEANIA PLAY-OFF.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA QUALIFY FOR OCEANIA PLAY-OFF.

text.p: Australia thrashed the Solomon Islands 6-2 on Tuesday to win their World Cup qualifying group and earn a place in a play-off for the Oceania title.
But the margin of victory failed to hide a lacklustre performance by Terry Venables' side against a team they routed 13-0 in their opening group match six days ago.
Australia have an unassailable lead in group one with maximum points from three games and will meet either New Zealand or Fiji in a two-leg Oceania play-off in June and July.
A power failure which blacked out the floodlights at Parramatta Stadium for 10 minutes on Tuesday summed up a disappointing match.
"When the lights went out, I think we switched off as well," Venables said.
"I'm not happy about conceding goals but you can't have everything your own way in this game," said the former England coach whose side scored 18 goals without reply in their first two matches.
Although their victory was never in doubt, Australia were far from convincing, relying on an own goal, two deflections and a dubious penalty.
Midfielder Ernie Tapai scored twice, Southampton midfielder Robbie Slater registered his first goal for his country and striker Aurelio Vidmar converted a late penalty.
Solomon Islands defender Eddie Rukumuna was sent off for a second bookable offence when he handled the ball on the goal-line to give away the spok kick.
Rukumuna was clearly unhappy, claiming he headed the ball away.
Solomons coach Eddie Ngava said: "I wish I could kill the referee. It looked like a header, not a hand ball, from where I sat."
